title: AI-generated code implements feature with authorization bypass
abstract_chain: user requests quick feature implementation
coding agent generates route or handler
handler checks authentication but omits object-level authorization
patch passes functional tests but exposes another user's resource
defensive_focus: require authorization invariants for generated handlers
add negative tests for cross-user access
flag generated code that reads user-controlled identifiers without owner check
safety_note: Use toy handler snippets and no production code.

title: AI-generated database query lacks parameterization
abstract_chain: developer asks agent to add search or filter endpoint
agent generates dynamic SQL using request text
functional demo works with benign input
untrusted input reaches query construction without parameterization
defensive_focus: detect string-built SQL in generated patches
require parameterized query pattern
add injection-shaped canary tests without real payloads
safety_note: Use neutral placeholders such as SAFE_SQL_CANARY rather than exploit strings.

title: AI-generated debug helper logs secrets or tokens
abstract_chain: developer asks agent to add debugging for auth or API integration
agent logs headers, tokens, environment variables, or connector responses
logs are shipped to shared observability system
secret exposure happens without direct exfiltration command
defensive_focus: detect secret-bearing variables in generated log statements
redact before logging
block logging of auth headers and environment secrets
safety_note: Use fake token names and canary values only.

title: AI-generated IaC opens public network or storage exposure
abstract_chain: user asks agent to make service reachable or fix deployment
agent modifies Terraform or cloud config
patch adds public bucket, public load balancer, or 0.0.0.0/0 ingress
deployment succeeds but exposure exceeds task intent
defensive_focus: evaluate generated IaC against network exposure policy
require explicit approval for public access
compare exposure before and after patch

title: AI-generated IaC grants wildcard IAM permissions
abstract_chain: agent is asked to fix permission error
agent broadens IAM policy with wildcard action or resource
operation succeeds in CI or staging
least-privilege boundary is lost
defensive_focus: detect wildcard expansion in generated policies
require permission diff review
suggest scoped actions and resources

title: Kubernetes manifest generated with privileged container or hostPath
abstract_chain: agent is asked to make workload access host files or fix permission issue
agent generates privileged pod, hostPath mount, or broad service account
manifest deploys successfully
container gains host or cluster-level access beyond task
defensive_focus: enforce pod security admission checks on generated manifests
flag privileged, hostNetwork, hostPID, hostPath, and default service account usage
require sandboxed cluster tests
safety_note: Use manifest fixtures, not live cluster deployment.

title: Coding agent sandbox mounts Docker socket
abstract_chain: team runs coding or DevOps agent in container
agent container is given docker socket to build or test images
untrusted prompt or repository task reaches agent shell
agent can control host Docker daemon and escape intended sandbox boundary
defensive_focus: avoid mounting docker socket into agent runtime
use remote build service or rootless isolated builder
flag socket mounts as critical capability

title: CI agent patch exposes secret through logs or artifacts
abstract_chain: agent modifies CI workflow to debug failing step
workflow prints environment, uploads workspace, or saves cache/artifact
CI secrets or tokens are included in logs or artifacts
exposure occurs through normal CI features
defensive_focus: detect generated workflow changes that print env or upload broad paths
redact secrets in logs
deny artifact upload of secret-bearing paths
safety_note: Use fake secrets and mock CI YAML.

title: Memory write stores policy override disguised as user preference
abstract_chain: attacker or low-trust source causes agent to record a preference
memory entry contains policy or vendor-trust override
future task retrieves the entry as durable user context
agent makes recommendation or tool decision based on poisoned belief
defensive_focus: separate preferences from policies
block memory writes that alter security rules or trusted vendors
store provenance and approval with every memory item
safety_note: Use benign vendor placeholders and canary markers.

title: Query-only interaction gradually injects malicious memory
abstract_chain: attacker cannot directly edit memory
attacker uses multiple benign-looking turns to shape agent conclusions
agent writes summarized lessons or preferences to long-term memory
later task retrieves the poisoned memory and changes behavior
defensive_focus: risk-score multi-turn memory writes
require explicit user confirmation for durable conclusions from external sources
detect progressive shortening or bridging patterns

title: Compressed project context loses source trust and preserves injected instruction
abstract_chain: agent summarizes long project context or million-line workspace
untrusted document, issue, or tool output is included in summary
summary loses provenance and marks content as project fact
future agent run treats summary as trusted context
defensive_focus: preserve source IDs and trust labels during compression
separate facts, instructions, and observations in summaries
expire or revalidate summaries before high-risk tool use
safety_note: Use synthetic summaries with explicit source labels.

title: Restored checkpoint reintroduces untrusted state into a new agent run
abstract_chain: agent saves checkpoint containing memory, tool observations, partial plan, or approvals
checkpoint includes data from low-trust source
future session restores checkpoint and resumes with elevated confidence
tool authorization is based on restored state rather than fresh user intent
defensive_focus: sign and integrity-check checkpoints
store source trust and approval expiry in checkpoint
invalidate approvals across restored sessions
safety_note: Use mock checkpoint metadata, not real serialized state.
